description:
FILED s406 (Opus 5), found by the #337 `my sub` probe battery and then narrowed.

SILENT WRONG:

    sub f { "F" }
    my $r1 = \&f;  my $r2 = \&f;
    print $r1 == $r2 ? "same" : "diff";      # perl: same    PCL: diff

perl gives the SAME CV every time `\&NAME` is evaluated, so the two references
are numerically equal.  PCL builds a new reference object per evaluation, so
`==` answers "diff" — silently, with no warning and no crash.

MEASURED, and it is NAMED SUBS ONLY (scratchpad cref/e1.pl):

    \%h  vs \%h      same / same     OK
    \@a  vs \@a      same / same     OK
    \$s  vs \$s      same / same     OK
    my $c = sub {…};  $c vs a copy   same / same     OK
    \&f  vs \&f      same / DIFF     <-- the bug

A stringified coderef IS stable (`my %h; $h{\&f} = 1; exists $h{\&f}` hits in
both), so hash keys work; it is the numeric identity that does not.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE PROBE: this is the same family as the Moo subclass
wall recorded in memory project_coderef_identity_blocker — Sub::Defer keys
%DEFERRED BY CODEREF and cross-checks `$deferred eq $deferred_sub`, and a
reference that is not identity-stable makes that lookup MISS.  Whether the two
have exactly the same cause is unmeasured; the probe above is the minimal one.

FIX SHAPE (not designed): `\&NAME` should hand back one cached reference per
resolved sub (the same object every time), the way perl hands back the CV.
Where: the runtime's `p-backslash-sub` and whatever `\&$name` /
`\&{"name"}` resolve through — they must share the cache, or the shapes
disagree.  Watch the case perl itself distinguishes: a sub REDEFINED after the
reference was taken keeps the OLD body under the old reference in some
spellings; probe before caching by name alone.

BAR: the five rows above, plus `\&f` taken before and after a redefinition,
plus a Moo board re-measure (task #208 territory) if the fix lands.


DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT TAKEN (s406, scratchpad cref/g1.pl) — the Sub::Defer
shape, so the "same family as the Moo wall" guess above is now MEASURED and
must be read narrowly:

    my $stub = sub { "STUB" };
    *{"Pkg::new"} = $stub;          # glob-install, as Sub::Defer does
    my $back  = \&Pkg::new;
    my $back2 = \&Pkg::new;

                              perl      PCL
    $stub == $back            same      same     <- the install/lookup pair WORKS
    $back == $back2           same      DIFF     <- the bug, and only this
    exists $DEFERRED{$back}   hit       hit      <- stringified keys are fine

So the ONE-install-ONE-lookup path Sub::Defer is described as using already
matches perl.  This task is the TWO-INDEPENDENT-LOOKUPS case.  The Moo wall
(project_coderef_identity_blocker) is the same bug ONLY IF Sub::Defer takes
\&NAME more than once for the same sub — unmeasured, and the cheap way to
settle it is to instrument undefer_sub rather than to reason about it.


CLOSED s407 (Fable review, e79f0a6) â THE CAUSE WAS NOT `\&NAME` IDENTITY.
p-backslash-sub returns (symbol-function sym), the same object every time, and
the exact reproducer answered "same" when both sides were boxes.  The emission
of the probe was the diagnosis: `$cr2`'s only use was `==`, so type flow froze it
to a RAW numeric slot â `(%pcl-to-number-strict (p-backslash-sub 'pl-f))` â and
%to-number-raw had no `functionp` arm: it answered 0 (the `(t 0)` swallow) while
the boxed side answered the object address.  A code ref is the ONE reference
that is a raw function rather than a wrapper box (\$x \@a \%h never reach the
raw path), which is why it looked like "named subs only".  Fix: the arm.  Guard:
Pl/t/ref-identity-01.t t21/t22.  All probes (e1, g1, exact repro, redefinition,
\&{"f"}, \&$n, alias, qualified) identical to perl.  The Moo %DEFERRED wall was
never this bug (the install/lookup shape already matched) â re-measure by board
(#208).  Lesson (DECIDED s407): a SILENT-WRONG task carries the EMISSION of its
reproducer.
subject: SILENT WRONG: `\&NAME` is a NEW reference every time - `\&f == \&f` is false (perl: true); named subs only, and the Sub::Defer/Moo wall is the same family
